html:
The fourth king of Joseon Korea, who ruled from 1418 to 1450. He is best known for creating Hangul, the Korean alphabet, and Koreans count him the greatest of their kings.

He gathered young scholars in a royal research institute, the Hall of Worthies, and put them to work on history, law, medicine, music and farming. A farming manual collected the methods of Korean farmers, suited to Korean soil and weather.

He also backed science and invention, much of it through the engineer Jang Yeong-sil, a man of low birth he promoted:

  • water clocks and sundials for public use;
  • the cheugugi rain gauge, used to measure rainfall across the kingdom;
  • improved astronomical instruments and a calendar fitted to Korea.

In the north his armies pushed back the Jurchens and set Korea's border roughly along the Yalu and Tumen rivers, where it still lies. He ruled through Neo-Confucian ideals of a wise, caring king. His face is on South Korea's 10,000 won note.
sum: The fourth king of Joseon Korea, who ruled from 1418 to 1450. He is best known for creating Hangul, the Korean alphabet, and Koreans count him the greatest of their kings.
